title: Wave-Particle Duality in Quantum Mechanics
text:
Quantum mechanics posits that all matter exhibits wave-particle duality. This fundamental principle suggests that particles, such as electrons and photons, are not restricted to behaving solely as point masses or pure waves; rather, they manifest properties of both depending on the experimental context in which they are measured.

The mathematical formulation describing this behavior often involves the de Broglie wavelength ($\lambda = h/p$), which relates a particle's momentum ($p$) to its associated wavelength ($\lambda$). This duality is most vividly illustrated by the double-slit experiment, where electrons fired at alternating intervals create an interference pattern characteristic only of waves passing through two slits simultaneously. The observation itself influences the outcome, suggesting that measurement is not a passive act.

Modern interpretations debate the physical reality of the wavefunction ($\psi$). Whether $\psi$ represents genuine physical substance or merely a mathematical descriptor of probability amplitude remains a central and unresolved discussion within physics, guiding theoretical efforts toward unifying quantum descriptions with general relativity.
